doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

chapter: Current gigs and Goodman family stories
title: Eubie Blake and Memories of You in the Goodman film
summary: Sol plays Memories of You, recalls Eubie Blake's birthday visits, and notes its use in the film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I can tell you never get tired of it.

That song was played three times in the Benny Goodman movie. I love that song. That was written by my dear friend Eubie Blake. He used to come to see me every birthday he had, for years and years my dear friend. He was a very close friend of mine, Eubie Blake. And when it was his birthday he came to see me, when he was like 98 years old, 99, I think he lived to about 101. And I always played “Memories of You” for him, it actually brought tears to my eyes when I played it for this man who was sitting in the audience, and he wrote the song. And then I’d play a song that he wrote called “I’m Just Wild About Harry,” and we would have the audience, I would have the audience sing [sings] “I’m just wild about Eubie,” you know that song? [Sol plays]. And then we’d get everybody singing that song. That was Harry Truman’s, by the way, that was his favorite song. “I’m Just Wild About Harry.”
Yeah. Makes for a good political song.
They played “Memories of You” in the Benny Goodman movie when the picture opened up, and then they played it again at the end of the movie, and they played it again during the Carnegie Hall scene.
Right. And Donna Reed comes in.
Right, Donna Reed walks in. They played it three times.

Yeah. She was a lovely lady by the way, Monk, she was a very, very warm, very fine lady. And we had some good times on the set with Buck Clayton, Ziggy Elman, Harry James. These guys are not around anymore.
Yeah. Well you’ve certainly brought some good cheer to many, many people over the years.
It’s great that you’re doing it, still. And I want to thank you for coming today.
